justification: The citation proof could not see control labels Ashfield prints as pictures numbered per part (PC4., DS5.1), so it could not prove or refuse them. This adds a local OCR read of those pictures, kept only when confident and label-shaped.

pre_impl.existing_data: No database writes. OCR probe on Ashfield chapter F pages 8-14: 24 of 24 labels read exactly. Corpus before: 4,511 of 16,291 unproven; wrong-label test 9 of 418 passing.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Expected OCR to clear most of Ashfield's unproven rows; it cleared 51 of 1,043, because most live Ashfield citations are composites the old reader invented, not unread labels.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends pdf_picture_labels, which already names pictures by counting; OCR only names what counting cannot.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Without the OCR engine installed the reader returns nothing and the proof behaves exactly as before.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change; the proof runs in the fidelity gate and the DQ-111 probe.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A misread label could prove a wrong citation. Mitigated: score at least 0.9, label-shaped text only, one reading per distinct picture; the wrong-label test stayed at 9 of 425.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a low-confidence or non-label reading is kept, one picture is read twice, or a missing OCR engine changes the reading
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Live: Ashfield unproven 1,043 to 994 (51 newly proven, 2 newly failing); wrong-label test 9 of 425 passing, same as before.

functions.name: pdf_picture_labels.ocr_label_pictures
functions.input: An open PyMuPDF document, one page, a cache keyed by picture mask, and a RapidOCR reader or None.
functions.output: (y, x, label) for each small picture read confidently as a label such as pc4. or ds5.1.
functions.if_none: With no reader, or a page whose images cannot be paired with their draws, returns an empty list.

values.name: OCR confidence
values.why: The 24 probed labels scored above it; low scores are misreads the proof must not trust.

break_it.scenario: OCR misreads a label, e.g. DS11.1 as DS1.1, with low confidence
break_it.what_happens: A wrong label could prove a citation that names the wrong control.
break_it.how: Readings under 0.9 confidence are dropped; the test pins it.

break_it.scenario: A small picture that is not a label, like an icon or the word Figure, is read
break_it.what_happens: Junk text would be inserted into the reading as if it were a label line.
break_it.how: Only text shaped like a label (letters then numbers) is kept.

break_it.scenario: The OCR engine is missing on a machine or in the Railway image
break_it.what_happens: The proof would crash, or silently behave differently from other environments.
break_it.how: The engine is optional and the reader returns nothing without it; it is now installed in the monitors image.

break_it.scenario: The same label picture appears on many pages and OCR is slow
break_it.what_happens: Reading every placement would make each chapter take minutes and could read one picture two ways.
break_it.how: Each distinct picture (by mask pixels) is read once and cached for the document.

break_it.scenario: A label picture is already named by counting under a Controls heading (Leichhardt)
break_it.what_happens: An OCR name and a counted name could disagree and insert two labels for one rule.
break_it.how: OCR names are used only for positions counting did not name.

post_merge.manual_verify: Railway rebuilds the monitors image with rapidocr-onnxruntime; the fidelity gate then reads Ashfield label pictures.
